caption: IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF DELMARVA POWER & LIGHT COMPANY FOR AN INCREASE IN ELECTRIC BASE RATES AND MISCELLANEOUS TARIFF CHANGES (FILED AUGUST 17, 2017).
title: DE PSC Docket 17-0977 — Order No. 10518
text:
BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE
IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF
DELMARVA POWER AND LIGHT COMPANY
FOR AN INCREASE IN ELECTRIC BASE
RATES AND MISCELLANEOUS TARIFF
CHANGES
(FILED AUGUST 17, 2017)
PSC DOCKET NO. 17-0977
ORDER NO. 10518
AND NOW, 
this 2U' day of August 2024, the Delaware Public Service Commission
("Commission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on August 17, 2017, Delmarva Power and Light Company (Delmarva" or
the "Company") filed an application ("Docket 17-0977") for an increase in electric distribution
rates; and
WHEREAS, on August 21, 2018, the Delaware Public Service Commission (the
"Commission") adopted Order No. 9248 in Docket No. 17-0977, which approved a settlement
agreement (the "Settlement Agreement") entered into by all parties in Docket 17-0977; and
WHEREAS, 
Section II. I .(c) of the Settlement Agreement addressed the impact of the Tax
Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA") and the process for how the Company's Excess Deferred
Income Taxes ("EDIT") would be flowed hack to customers; specifically, $44.3 million of non
protected property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a six-year amortization period, and
$20.8 million of non-protected non-property related EDIT was to he flowed hack using a five-year
amortization period;' and
' 
$62.5 million and $29.3 million respectively when grossed up by the revenue conversion factor of 1.40926.

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
WHEREAS, on June 25, 2024, Delmarva filed an application (the "Application") to
modify its electric Rider "EDIT" Excess Deferred Income Tax Credit ("Rider EDIT"); and
WHEREAS, Delmarva intends to reset to zero ($0.000000) certain Rider EDIT service
elassifications whose EDIT liability balanees have been fully credited to the respective customers;
and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section II.l.(c)(vii) of the Settlement Agreement, because the
amounts due to the customers in each service elassification could not be calculated precisely at the
time of the Settlement Agreement, the parties agreed that any amounts paid to customers in excess
of the total EDIT balance will be recorded as a regulatory asset with a return at the Company's
Commission authorized rate of return to be recovered in the Company's subsequent rate case; and
WHEREAS, 
Delmarva has requested similar treatment to that received in PSC Order No.
10135, issued December 14, 2022, PSC Order No. 10179, issued February 22, 2023, PSC Order
No. 10282, issued August 23, 2023, and PSC Order No. 10338, issued November 29, 2023, that
instead of carrying a regulatory asset balance for the five-year EDIT credits, any regulatory asset
balance be transferred to the respective six-year regulatory liability balance to reduce the
remaining liability if that balanee still has a credit; and
WHEREAS, 
per Schedule 1 of the Application, the General Service Primary ("GSP") five-
year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully eredited to the rate class by end of August 2024. The
Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate elass to zero effective September 1,
2024; and
WHEREAS, 
per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Medium General Service - Secondary
("MGS-S") five-year EDIT balanee is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
September 2024. The Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective October 1, 2024; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Outdoor Recreational Lighting
("ORL") six-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
November 2024. The Company intends to set the six-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective December 1, 2024; and
WHEREAS, 
the Company requests authority to transfer any regulatory asset balances for
the GSP and MGS-S five-year EDIT credits to the respective six-year EDIT liability balances, thus
reducing the respective six-year EDIT liability balances; and
WHEREAS, Staff submitted a memorandum to the Commission recommending that 1)
the five-year EDIT credits for the GSP and MGS-S rate classes be set to zero effective September
1, 2024, and October 1, 2024, respectively, and that any regulatory asset balances for these two
rate classes be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability balances; and 2) the six-year
EDIT credit for the ORL rate class be set to zero effective December 1, 2024, and any regulatory
asset balance for this rate class be addressed in the Company's next rate case;
NOW, 
THEREFORE, 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT FEWER THAN THREE COMMISSIONERS:
1. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the GSP rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective September 1, 2024.
2. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the GSP rate
class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
3. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the MGS-S rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective October 1, 2024.

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
4. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the MGS-S
rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
5. 
That the six-year EDIT credit for the ORE rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective December 1, 2024
6. 
That any regulatory asset balances resulting from the six-year EDIT credit for the
ORE rate class will be addressed in Delmarva's next rate case.
7. 
Delmarva is hereby notified that it will be assessed the costs of this proceeding
pursuant to 26 Del. C. § 114(b).
8. 
The Commission reserves the jurisdiction and authority to enter such further orders
in this matter as may be deemed necessary or proper.
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
